did_you_know.text: Did you know? Belshazzar held a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and during the feast he drank wine in front of them all.
Did you know? Belshazzar ordered the gold and silver vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem to be brought, so that the king, his nobles, and his wives could drink from them.
Did you know? The guests at the feast praised idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone—but not the God who held their lives and all their ways in his hand.
Did you know? At that very moment, the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the wall of the palace opposite the lampstand. Belshazzar saw the writing hand and was terrified.
Did you know? The king promised that whoever could read the writing and explain it would be dressed in purple, receive a gold chain, and be made the third-highest ruler in the kingdom.
Did you know? The queen reminded Belshazzar about Daniel, who was known for his wisdom, understanding, and exceptional spirit, and recommended that he be brought before the king.
Did you know? Daniel told Belshazzar that he was not interested in the gifts and honors the king offered him; he agreed only to read the writing and explain it.
Did you know? Daniel accused Belshazzar of knowing everything that had happened to Nebuchadnezzar, yet still refusing to humble himself.

Did you know? The writing on the wall consisted of three words: “Mene, Mene, Tekel, and Parsin.” Daniel explained that Belshazzar’s kingdom had been counted and brought to an end, that he had been weighed and found wanting, and that his kingdom would be divided and given to the Medes and Persians.
Did you know? Although Belshazzar honored Daniel and gave him a high position, that very night Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, was killed.
